items.e: **Silka daatach** amina The Talmud is full of these [statements] that you might think at the beginning so, and then at the end, it concludes the opposite. And apparently we have a question for the redactor, why did they lay out what you might have thought, if it isn’t even the truth! They should have told us from the beginning what the conclusion of the matter is! But know this, that not a single thing is recalled for nought in our holy Talmud, and it is all truth. And even though the silka daatach, the “you might think” does not remain in the conclusion for this particular matter, in any case, the reasoning of the “you might think” is still true for some other matter….

How many kindnesses has the Omnipresent bestowed upon us! And it is upon us to praise the Lord of all who created the world for us. He set aside and created and crafted and made for us. And the world endures and exists on his Torah. Which he gave us through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the faithful member of his household. And he transmitted it to Joshua his attendant. And Joshua transmitted it to the elders of his congregation. And from the elders to the prophets of the congregation of Jacob, his allotted portion. And from the prophets to the men of the Great Assembly, who restored the crown to its ancient glory. And even though we walk in Exile. We nevertheless have our tradition
